dossier.scp_unleashed.151.title: The Painting
dossier.scp_unleashed.151.caption: SCP-151 at intake. The photographer was told not to linger.

page.title: Special Containment Procedures:
text: SCP-151 is kept on its own easel in a locked viewing room with a single door. It cannot be lodged in a standard storage container and must not be taken off the easel.

Viewing is limited to short, supervised glances at the painted side. Any person who reports shortness of breath must be turned away from SCP-151 at once and given time to recover before any further viewing.

page.title: Description:
text: SCP-151 is an oil painting of a breaking ocean wave beneath a dark horizon, on a plain wooden studio easel. The canvas is unsigned and its brushwork is competent but unremarkable.

Persons who keep their eyes on the painted side report the taste of salt water, then find that they cannot draw breath, exactly as if they were deep underwater. A viewer who does not look away will drown on dry land.
Breath returns only slowly after the viewer looks away, far more slowly than it would for a swimmer reaching the surface.

page.title: Addendum 151-1: Viewing Log
text: Test 151-02: a researcher viewed SCP-151 from across the room. Breathing failed within seconds and took most of a minute to return.
Test 151-05: a D-Class subject viewed SCP-151 through a reinforced glass window. The effect was unchanged.
Test 151-09: D-9341 viewed SCP-151 for twenty minutes without any reaction, and collapsed when viewing it again the next day. %rThe difference is under review.%r

page.title: Addendum 151-2: Provenance
page.text: SCP-151 has no recovery record. It was delivered to a reader of this file by the individual in Foundation dress described in the files of other objects, who would not look at it while handing it over. See field notes.
